tested_scope: One bounded official-GitHub-documentation leaf on whether the automatically generated immutable-release attestation remains a usable historical tombstone after release deletion and whether its identity/retrieval semantics are documented across repository rename or transfer.

public_sources.observation: GitHub documents that publishing an immutable release automatically generates a cryptographically verifiable release attestation containing the release tag, commit SHA, and release assets. GitHub also documents tag-name non-reuse after deleting such a release and repository-resurrection protection. The page does not state that the generated release attestation remains retrievable after the release is deleted or define rename/transfer identity semantics for it.

The documented verification flow begins by verifying that a release exists and is immutable via gh release verify RELEASE-TAG. No historical verification flow for a deleted immutable release is documented on this page.

For generic artifact attestations, GitHub documents repository-scoped finding/deletion and states that a deleted attestation can no longer be found on GitHub. It recommends deleting attestations for artifacts that no longer exist. This demonstrates that generic attestation presence is not inherently permanent, but this leaf did not establish that automatically generated immutable-release attestations have exactly the same deletion lifecycle.

The repository attestation REST endpoint lists attestations by subject SHA-256 digest associated with a repository and is usable without authentication for public resources. The documented interface does not expose a historical immutable-release lookup keyed by deleted release/tag reservation, nor does it specify rename/transfer continuity for release attestations.

GitHub documents that releases and settings transfer with a repository, but this transfer page does not document immutable-release attestation identity, historical attestation lookup continuity, or attestation subject remapping across owner/name changes.

GitHub documents artifact attestations as available for public repositories on GitHub Free, Pro, and Team, but this page concerns workflow-generated artifact attestations and does not prove that the automatic immutable-release attestation or its historical retention has a zero-finite-quota contract.

results.strongest_positive: The automatic release attestation binds release tag, commit SHA, and release assets, and GitHub separately provides attestation lookup by subject digest for repository-associated attestations.
results.falsification: The official documentation retrieved in this bounded leaf does not establish that an immutable-release attestation survives release deletion as a retrievable object, remains addressable after repository rename/transfer, or has a stable historical identity independent of current repository naming. Therefore it cannot yet serve as the durable anti-replay tombstone witness required by the current candidate protocol.
results.observation_inference_boundary: Observed documentation facts are limited to the statements above. It is an inference, not a documented fact, that generic artifact-attestation lifecycle rules might apply to automatic immutable-release attestations; this inference is not used as a positive acceptance claim.

phase1_acceptance.scope_guard: Only current multi_agent role-local LATEST plus official public GitHub documentation were semantic inputs; no O, other-role, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, scheduler, or protected-primary semantic input/effect was used.

conflict_check.basis: Continuation came from current role-local LATEST and the leaf used only official public documentation; no other worker scope was read or claimed.

unresolved_child: A historical witness still needs an incarnation identity that survives rename/transfer but distinguishes delete-and-recreate, without relying on finite quota or richer-mode arbitration.
exact_continuation: Part115: execute one bounded official-GitHub documentation leaf on repository incarnation identity. Test whether repository numeric id/node_id remains stable across rename and transfer, whether delete-and-recreate with the same owner/name receives a distinct identity, and whether that identity is exposed through zero-cost, zero-finite-quota Chat-accessible repository reads. Evaluate pairing that incarnation key with immutable-release tag reservation as a historical tombstone binding. If any identity-stability or quota-zero obligation is undocumented, fail closed and persist a distinct next candidate without executing a second leaf in the same invocation.
